haiku-low.q1: Row count of 10,000 or fewer: CSV streams in the same HTTP response, nothing stored. More than 10,000: a report_exports row is queued, a background job builds the file, and the user gets an emailed link.
haiku-low.q2: The API returns the active export with 202 and the same JSON shape, instead of starting a new one. Its filters and cols may differ from the user's view; this is Decision 2.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works 24 hours, created at send time. The exports bucket's 7-day lifecycle rule deletes the file, and the page then shows expired. No cleanup job exists.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, retried after 60 s and 300 s. After the last failure, the row is set to failed, the upload aborted, and an export_failed email sent. The page shows the failure.
haiku-low.q5: Only the replica. Report rows are never read from the primary, and the row_count read also comes from the replica.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table on the primary database. The page calls the latest-export endpoint on load and polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, so reopening shows current state.
haiku-low.q7: It streams 5,000-row keyset pages into a 16 MB buffer, uploading each full buffer as a multipart part, about 57 parts. Only one page and one buffer are held. Figures are estimates until Step 12 measures them.
haiku-low.q8: Parts stay in an open, invisible multipart upload. The next attempt aborts it, and the bucket discards it after 24 hours. Each retry restarts from the beginning, keeping no progress.
haiku-low.q9: Stored as raw filters and cols in the report_exports row when the click is recorded. The job payload holds only export_id, so the job reads them from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for queued or running rows. A losing insert breaks it, so the request reads and returns the winning row.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete with state done and object_key set, after complete_multipart. A rerun with email_sent_at empty resends the email only; otherwise it stops without redoing the file.
haiku-low.q12: If it fails before the first byte, the API returns 503. If it drops partway, the connection breaks; fetch lets the page show an error. Nothing is stored and no retry occurs.

sonnet.q1: The server reads reports.row_count from the replica. If 10,000 or fewer, it builds the CSV and streams it in the same HTTP response (text/csv attachment, nothing stored). If more than 10,000, it records a report_exports row, queues a background job, and returns 202 with JSON {export_id, state, filters, cols}; the job builds the file in the exports bucket and the user gets an email with a 24-hour download link (page also shows progress and a Download button).
sonnet.q2: The POST returns the existing active export (same JSON shape, with that export's own filters and cols, which may differ from what the user is viewing) instead of starting a new one, unless it is stale (queued with no job_id for over 5 minutes, or running with updated_at over 2 hours old), in which case it is marked failed 'stalled' and a new export is started. Rejecting with 409 is an unconfirmed alternative (Decision 2).
sonnet.q3: The emailed signed URL works for 24 hours from when it is created at send time. The exports bucket lifecycle rule deletes each object 7 days after creation. The page can issue a fresh 24-hour link via the download endpoint while the file exists.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s then 300 s). After the last fails, on_final_failure aborts any open upload, sets the row to failed with a short error, and sends the export_failed email with {export_id, report_id}. The page reads the row, so it shows the failure message and a Start again button even if the email fails. (If the row is done but the email never sent, it retries export_ready instead.)
sonnet.q5: The read replica. Report rows are never read from the primary (reports.row_count is also read from the replica). The report_exports metadata table lives on the primary.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table (column state: queued, running, done, failed) on the primary database. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load, which returns the user's active export or else the most recent one, so reopening later shows current state. While queued or running, the page polls that endpoint every 5 seconds.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads keyset pages of 5,000 rows from the replica, encodes CSV into an in-memory buffer, and uploads each 16 MB buffer as a multipart part (about 57 parts for roughly 900 MB), keeping only etags in memory, then completes the upload. Only one page and one 16 MB buffer are held at a time, which should be far under 512 MB. This is an estimate until Step 12 measures it; it must also finish within the 1,800 s attempt timeout (about 0.5 MB/s).
sonnet.q8: The multipart upload stays open and invisible, so nothing is visible at the final key and no partial file can be downloaded. The next attempt aborts the old upload (ignoring errors) and starts over from the beginning at Step 6 (no progress is kept); the bucket also discards uncompleted uploads after 24 hours. Resume is not part of the plan (Decision 4).
sonnet.q9: In the report_exports row's filters and cols columns (raw, validated query strings), written when the row is inserted. The job payload carries only {"export_id": ...} (queue payload limit is 64 KB); the handler loads the row by export_id and uses the stored filters and cols via the shared module.
sonnet.q10: The database: a partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) for rows whose state is queued or running. If an insert violates it, the API reads the winning row and returns it, so both responses carry the same export_id.
sonnet.q11: Before the email: the file must be complete (complete_multipart succeeded) and the row set to done with object_key and finished_at; then a signed URL is made at send time and send_email called, after which email_sent_at is set. If the job runs again: if state is done, it skips the export and only resends the email if email_sent_at is empty, then stops; if state is failed it stops. So no second copy or second email when email_sent_at is set.
sonnet.q12: If the replica fails before the first byte, the API returns 503 and the user can click again. If it fails mid-stream, the connection drops; because the page downloads with fetch (not a plain link), the page gets an error it can show instead of a silently truncated file. Nothing is stored.
